<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|155}}</noinclude>eares: as did the False-Prophets, when they were magnified and commended therfore of the carnal Iewes.

''35. Lend, hoping nothing.''] In that vve may here seeme to be moued to lend to those vvhom vve thinke not able nor like euer to repay againe, it must be holden for a counsel rather then a commaundement, except the case of necessitie. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Against vsurie.}}but it may be taken rather for a precept, wherein vsurie, that is to say, the expectation not of the money lent, but of vantage for lone, is forbidden: as by other places of Scripture it is condemned, and is a thing against the Lavv of nature and nations. And greate shame and pitie it is, that it should be so much vsed or suffered among Christians, or so couered and cloked vnder the habite of other contractes, as it is.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. VII.}}}}}}

{{c|''He testifieth, the faith of the Centurion who was a Gentil, to be greater then he found among al the Iewes, and cureth his seruant absent. 11. the vvidovves sonne he reuiueth and restoreth to her, and is renowmed therevpon. 18. To Iohns messengers he answereth vvith miracles, leauing to Iohn to preach thereby vnto them that he is Christ. 24. And afterward he declareth how vvorthy credit was Iohns testimonie, 29. inueighing against the Pharisees, 31. who vvith neither of their maners of liuing could be wonne. 36. shewing also vnto them by occasion of Marie Magdalen, how he is a frende to sinners, not to maintaine them in sinne, but to forgiue them their sinnes vpon their faith and penance.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=7|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 8, 5.''}}* vvhen he had fully said al his vvords into the eares of the people, he entred into Capharnaum. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=2}}† And the seruant of a certaine Centurion being sicke, vvas readie to die: vvho vvas deere vnto him. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=3}}† And when he had heard of {{sc|Iesvs}}, he sent vnto him the Auncients of the Ievves, desiring him to come and heale his seruant. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=4}}† But they being come to {{sc|Iesvs}}, besought him earnestly, saying to him, That he is vvorthie that thou shouldest doe this for him. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=5}}† for he loueth our nation: and he hath {{sup|‖}} built a synagogue for vs. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=6}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} went with them. And vvhen he vvas novv not farre from the house, the Centurion sent his frends vnto him, saying, Lord, trouble not thy self. for {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annotations vpon S. Matth. c. 8, 8.}}∷ ''I am not vvorthie that thou shouldest enter vnder my roofe''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=7}}† for the vvhich cause neither did I thinke my self vvorthie to come to thee: but say the vvord, and my seruant shal be made whole. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=8}}† for I also am a man subiect to authoritie, hauing vnder me souldiars: and I say to this, goe, and he goeth: and to an other, come, and he commeth: and to my seruant, doe this, and he doeth it. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=9}}† Which {{sc|Iesvs}} hearing, marueiled: and turning to the multitudes that folovved him he said, Amen I say to you, neither in Israel haue I found so great faith. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=10}}† And they that vvere sent, being returned home, found the seruant that had been sicke, vvhole.<noinclude>{{rh||V ij|And}}</noinclude>
